key_facts: MAJOR SATURDAY QUALIFYING & SPRINT UPDATE Aug 8 (T+1d to Sunday Aug 9 Silverstone 20-lap main GP): Jorge Martin 0.15->0.36 (+0.21), Ai Ogura 0.14->0.21 (+0.07), Raul Fernandez 0.17->0.14 (-0.03), Marco Bezzecchi 0.21->0.09 (-0.12), ADDED Alex Marquez 0.07 replacing Marc Marquez (0.10->~0.052 outside); sum=0.87, outside=0.13 (Marc Marquez ~0.052, Fabio Di Giannantonio ~0.048, Pedro Acosta ~0.013, rest ~0.017; total ~80% Aprilia / ~17% Ducati / ~3% others). KEY AUG 8 SILVERSTONE EVIDENCE (MotoGP.com, Crash.net, Motorsport.com, Autosport, BikeSport News, Reuters): (1) HISTORIC APRILIA LOCKOUT IN BOTH Q2 & SPRINT: Aprilia swept the front row (P1 Martin 1:56.160 new lap record, P2 Raul Fernandez +0.021s, P3 Ogura +0.189s; P5 Bezzecchi +0.296s) AND swept their first-ever MotoGP Sprint 1-2-3 (Martin P1 19:49.066, Ogura P2 +1.530s, Bezzecchi P3 +3.974s), finishing 3.0s-7.0s ahead of the best Ducati (Alex Marquez P4 +6.956s) in just 10 laps. (2) JORGE MARTIN SURGES TO CLEAR FAVORITE (0.36): Championship leader (+17 pts over Ogura) found another step with Aprilia's latest aero tweaks, smashed the lap record for pole, nailed the launch, led every lap of the Sprint, fended off Ogura mid-race, and pulled clear by 1.53s late. Healthy, clean-air pole advantage; capped at 0.36 by 3 fast RS-GP26 teammates, 20-lap Medium rear switch, ~13% crash/DNF rate, and Silverstone weather risk. (3) AI OGURA CLEAR #2 (0.21): Healthy #2 in championship, P3 front-row start (338 km/h speed trap), held P2 off the line, fought off Diggia, pressured Martin mid-race for clean P2 (+1.530s), and elite 20-lap tyre conserver. (4) RAUL FERNANDEZ #3 DESPITE SPRINT CRASH (0.14): Qualified P2 just +0.021s off Martin's lap record and posted Friday's best Medium-tyre long-run average (1:58.585), healthy on front row; trimmed from 0.17 after poor Sprint launch (P2->P6) and Lap 4/5 front-end tip-off at Turn 4 in dirty air behind Bezzecchi (costing Sprint tyre/setup data). (5) MARCO BEZZECCHI CUT TO #4 (0.09): Heroic P3 (+3.974s) from P5 grid after passing Marc and hunting down Diggia, BUT backed off late in Q2 (lost rear aero + injury) and was in tears after just 10 laps post-collarbone & knee surgery (missing kneecap bone fragment) -- doubling to 20 laps Sunday from Row 2 poses extreme endurance risk. (6) ALEX MARQUEZ TAKES #5 OVER MARC & DIGGIA (0.07): Top Ducati in Sprint (P4 +6.956s, healthy, 2025 Silverstone Sprint winner, P1 FP1, P7 grid), comfortably passing both Marc and rear-grip-stricken Diggia (P5 +8.651s from P4 grid). Marc Marquez (P6 grid) suffered catastrophic rear-grip collapse to P9 (+13.965s, passed by Alex, Acosta, Mir, Morbidelli; kept at ~0.052 outside mainly for wet-weather/Medium-tyre bounce-back ceiling). Bagnaia P16 grid / P17 Sprint (+23.7s).
